name: LA-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Troy Carter running with $1.4M raised
Republican challenger Peter Williams has no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~98%
model.rationale: This New Orleans-based seat's D+25 lean plus Carter's incumbency and strong fundraising against an unfunded challenger make a Democratic win overwhelming; markets agree at roughly 98%. No polls or expert ratings exist, but fundamentals alone justify Safe D.
model.watch: Any late outside spending or a polling surprise showing a tighter race would be the first sign of movement, though none is currently visible.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Troy Carter, the Democratic incumbent in this New Orleans-centered district, is seeking another term against Republican Peter Williams, a Libertarian, an independent, and a minor Democratic candidate. The district's D+25 partisan lean makes it one of the most Democratic seats in Louisiana, and Carter enters with about $1.4 million raised and $383,000 on hand. Williams reports no fundraising, and no outside groups are active in the race.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the contest, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and prediction markets, which price a Carter win near 98%. With a heavily Democratic electorate, a well-funded incumbent, and an under-resourced challenger, the seat is rated Safe Democratic.
